item.title: AVS Uri: Calculation of annuity and contribution gaps
item.description: First Uri pillar: compensation fund, calculation of the AVH annuity and supplementary benefits for contribution gaps and minimum living allowance.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The cantonal compensation fund manages the first pillar AVS at the local level - Each missing year of contributions reduces the monthly pension by about 2-3% - Supplementary benefits supplement insufficient pensions up to the minimum subsistence level
## Key facts - **What**: First pillar AVS and supplementary benefits in the Canton of Uri - Who: Active residents and pensioners who contribute or receive pensions - Contributions: 5.3% employee (10.6% total with employer) - Management: Cantonal compensation fund Uri, coordinated by the BSV/UFAS - Minimum: Supplementary benefits for those who do not reach the cantonal minimum subsistence level - Gaps: Years without contributions reduce the calculated pension
In the Canton of Uri, as in every Swiss canton, the first pillar of the pension system — the AVS (Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance) — rests on three pillars: the systematic collection of mandatory contributions, the faithful recording of each year of contribution, and the integration through supplementary benefits for those with insufficient income. 📊 All this is coordinated by an institution often unknown to contributors: the cantonal compensation fund, the local administrative office that acts as a link between the hundreds of thousands of active workers and the pensioners who depend on their future pension.
The cantonal compensation fund is neither a bank nor an investment fund. It is a federal-cantonal office that collects the mandatory contributions of 5.3% from employees (and 10.6% total including employer payments), maintains the permanent and individual register of each contributor, and distributes both ordinary pensions and supplementary benefits for those who do not reach the minimum subsistence level. In the Canton of Uri, this function is managed by the local fund, coordinated at the national level by the Federal Social Insurance Office (UFAS/BSV).
### The role of the cantonal compensation fund
When a resident of the Canton of Uri starts working, their compensation fund opens a permanent individual account. Each month, the employer pays the contributions (5.3% + 5.3%) to the AVS budget. The fund records: year, gross salary amount, days worked, any gaps (non-working periods). This archive is essential because the final pension is not an arbitrary figure, but the result of a federal formula that multiplies: number of complete contribution years (ideal: 44 years for men, 43 for women), average salary of the entire career, seniority multiplier (varies with the current reference age).
If during the working life a year without contributions emerges — due to uncovered unemployment, illness, studies, or absences from the labor market — that gap is recorded as a contribution gap. A single gap of a full year reduces the pension by about 2-3% compared to the theoretical maximum. Two gaps mean a double reduction. For those who have had a fragmented career (emigrations, country changes, interruptions for care), gaps can accumulate and lead to pensions significantly lower than expected.
The cantonal compensation fund has the legal obligation to inform each insured person of the gaps detected before retirement, and to communicate what remedies exist: voluntary contributions, supplementary benefits, or a combination of both. ## # How Contribution Gaps Affect Rent Calculation
The monthly AVS income is proportional to three factors, all managed by the cantonal compensation fund:
1. Number of years of contribution
The formula provides for a “standard” number of years: 44 for men, 43 for women (stylized, evolving data). Those who have worked all these years receive an income calculated on a full average salary. Those who have less (e.g. 40 years instead of 44) receive a proportionally reduced amount. Each missing year subtracts about 2-3% from the total.
**2. Average career salary **
The fund calculates the average gross income for all years of contribution. A higher average salary = higher income. This average income is revalued each year according to the federal wage index (revaluation factor of the AVS, updated annually by the Confederation).
3. Impact of Gaps: Bridging vs. Accepting Reductions
If there have been years of non-contribution during the career, the fund offers two paths: voluntary contributions (retroactively paying contributions for the missing years, calculated on the average income of that period — this fills the gap in the record and increases the calculated income), or supplementary benefits (if the voluntary payments are not economically sustainable, the cantonal supplementary benefits supplement the income up to the living minimum).

## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Access to Supplementary Benefits: Step-by-Step Operational Guide
Cantonal supplementary benefits are the safety net for those with insufficient AHV pension. In the Canton of Uri, they are governed by cantonal ordinances that define amounts, eligibility criteria, and application procedures. The cantonal compensation fund manages the applications.
**Step 1: Check General Eligibility**
You are entitled to supplementary benefits if: your monthly AHV pension (alone) is below the minimum living standard defined by the Canton of Uri (specific amount not available in this guide; consult the fund directly), your personal assets (bank accounts, additional real estate, investments) do not exceed the maximum threshold set by cantonal law, you reside in the Canton of Uri (official residence for >90 days per year).
Step 2: Gather Documentation
Before submitting your application, prepare: AHV account statement (request a complete copy from the fund or print from the federal portal myAVS with federal credentials); estimated pension calculation (the fund sends this to you automatically 4 weeks before retirement; if you don't have it, request it); income declaration for the last 2 years (cantonal forms or copy of the declaration to the municipality); residence certificate (issued by the municipality of residence, valid for 3 months); bank account statement (balance as of December 31 of the previous year for all accounts in Switzerland and abroad); documentation of extraordinary expenses (rents, medical care not covered, legitimate creditor debts, if relevant).
Step 3: Submit the Application
1. Download the cantonal form for supplementary benefits from the website of the State Chancellery of the Canton of Uri or request it from the local fund. 2. Fill out the form in all sections (personal data, incomes, assets, special expenses). 3. Attach all the documentation mentioned above. 4. Submit the application in person at the Uri compensation fund or send it by registered mail with attachments. 5. Keep a copy of the deposit receipt.
Step 4: Application Review and Decision
The fund will verify your data (contact municipalities, asset checks, with the Federal Customs Administration and the SNB for foreign accounts). Average response time: 2-4 weeks (if all documentation is complete). You will receive a decision letter with the calculation: AHV pension + supplementary benefit amount = total monthly amount recognized. If the application is accepted, payments start the month following approval.
Step 5: Annual Review
Supplementary benefits are not automatically permanent. They must be reviewed annually, as your assets may change, your additional incomes may vary, the cantonal minimum living standard may be indexed. The fund will send you an annual review form: complete it and return the updated documents to maintain your entitlement to benefits.
### Where to Find Help and Online Tools
The [AHV calculator of the Confederation](nav:calculator) allows you to estimate the expected pension by entering years of contribution and average salary. This is useful for identifying gaps and planning voluntary payments before retirement.
For specific questions about the Uri minimum living standard, exact asset criteria, or additional amounts, contact the Uri cantonal compensation fund directly (address on the State Chancellery website). [Access the AHV calculator to estimate your future pension and plan supplementary payments](nav:pension).

item.title: Appenzell Innerrhoden inheritance tax
item.description: Inheritance and gift taxation in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden: rates by degree of kinship, exemptions for spouses and descendants, declaration procedures and cantonal deadlines.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - In the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, inheritance and gift tax is regulated by autonomous cantonal laws - Spouse and descendants benefit from specific exemptions - The declaration follows precise deadlines established by the cantonal tax administration
## Key facts - **What**: Inheritance and donation tax in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden - Who: Cantonal tax administration of Appenzell Innerrhoden - Where: Canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden (northeast Switzerland) - Degree of kinship: Spouse, descendants, ascendants, others - Exemptions: Provided for spouse and descendants - Declaration: Cantonal specific procedures and terms
In the Swiss canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, as in the other twenty-six cantons, taxation on inheritances and donations is regulated by its own cantonal regulations. The Swiss tax system works on three levels - federal, cantonal and municipal - and as regards inheritance and gift taxes, responsibility lies entirely with the cantonal authorities. Each canton establishes rates, exemptions and procedures independently.
Inheritance taxation in Appenzell Innerrhoden provides three key elements: rates differentiated by degree of kinship, specific exemptions for spouses and descendants, and a declaration procedure with precise deadlines to be respected.
### The cantonal system of Appenzell Innerrhoden
In the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, inheritance and gift tax is administered by the cantonal tax authorities. Unlike direct federal tax (IFD), which has uniform rates and rules at national level, inheritance tax remains the responsibility of the cantons. This means that any taxpayer who inherits property in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden must comply with the specific rates and rules of that canton.
The Swiss tax structure provides that the cantonal administration defines the tax rates depending on the degree of kinship between the deceased and the heir, the exemptions or reductions for certain categories of heirs, the terms and methods of declaration, and the terms of payment of the tax due.
### Taxation overview
In the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, the general principle is that the closer the family relationship with the deceased, the lower the tax burden. The surviving spouse typically benefits from broad exemptions, as do children and other descendants, while ascendants (parents, grandparents) and more distant relatives are subject to progressively higher rates. Finally, non-relatives are generally subjected to the maximum rates.
However, the specific details — the exact rates, the exemption thresholds, the progression coefficients — vary from canton to canton. To find out the precise rates and rules of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, it is necessary to consult the cantonal tax administration and the cantonal [dichiarazione imposte](nav:tax-return) directly. ### Degree of kinship and rates
In most Swiss cantons, including Appenzell Innerrhoden, the inheritance tax system is based on the degree of kinship. This classification determines which heirs pay less taxes and which pay more.
**Surviving spouse**: The deceased's spouse generally benefits from inheritance tax exemption, or at very reduced rates. This is a well-established principle in Swiss law, recognized in almost all cantons. The logic is that the spouse is the continuer of the family and family assets.
Descendants (children, grandchildren): Direct descendants — children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren — are also favored over other categories of heirs. They often benefit from partial exemptions or lower rates than ascendants or collaterals. The closer the line of descent to the deceased, the lower the tax usually is.
Ascendants and collaterals. Parents, grandparents, brothers and sisters are taxed at intermediate rates. They do not receive the reductions granted to spouses and descendants, but are still favored over non-relatives.
Not relatives. People who are not related to the deceased, such as friends, unmarried partners (in some cantons) or colleagues, are subject to the maximum rates.
Exact rates vary by canton: for details specific to Appenzell Innerrhoden, see the cantonal [dichiarazione imposte](nav:tax-return).
### Tax exemptions and benefits
The canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, like all Swiss cantons, provides specific exemptions for certain heirs. The most common exemptions concern the surviving spouse and direct descendants, especially minor children.
The spousal exemption reflects the principle that the surviving partner should not be penalized taxally at the time of inheritance. This promotes family continuity and the economic stability of the family.
For descendants, exemptions can be total (for amounts up to a certain threshold) or partial (reduced rate). Some cantons provide different exemptions for older children than for younger ones, or for grandchildren depending on their economic situation.
### Exemption procedure
To qualify for an exemption, the heir must usually declare his or her status and relationship to the deceased in the inheritance declaration form. The cantonal tax administration then checks whether the requirements for the exemption exist. Documents such as a marriage certificate, birth certificate and will are necessary to prove the relationship and the deceased's wishes.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Declaration procedure
In the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, the successor (heir or executor) must declare the succession to the cantonal tax administration within a deadline established by cantonal law. This deadline is typically between three and six months after the deceased's death, although the rules vary by canton.
The succession declaration must include personal data of the heir and the deceased, a detailed list of inherited assets (real estate, bank accounts, securities, furniture, etc.), total value of the inheritance, calculation of the tax due based on cantonal rates, and any claims for exemptions or reductions.
### Deadlines and terms to be respected
Compliance with reporting deadlines is critical. A late filing may result in penalties and interest. Some cantons grant an automatic extension if the succession is still being settled (for example, if the will is contested in court), but generally the deadline is non-negotiable.
After submitting the declaration, the cantonal tax administration notifies the amount of tax due. The heir then has a further deadline (generally 30-60 days) to pay the tax. Failure to pay within the deadline entails legal interest and potential debt collection actions.
### What to do concretely
If you inherit an estate in the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden, here are the steps to follow:
1. Collect documents: Death certificate of the heir, will, marriage/birth certificates, property documents (real estate, accounts, titles).
2. Contact the cantonal tax administration: The tax office of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden provides declaration forms and clarifications on local deadlines, applicable rates and available exemptions.
3. Fill in the [dichiarazione imposte](nav:tax-return): Use the official form of the canton to declare the inheritance and request any exemptions.
4. Calculate the tax: Apply the cantonal rates (which vary by degree of kinship) to the net value of the inheritance.
5. Pay within the deadlines: Pay the amount due within the deadline set by the administration.
6. Keep receipts: Keep copies of all payment documents and correspondence with the tax office for future reference.
### Tools and resources
For those who wish to find out more about the specific tax situation of their inheritance, it is advisable to contact the tax administration of the canton of Appenzell Innerrhoden directly. A tax advisor or a lawyer specializing in inheritance law can help with complex inheritances. Also review our [dichiarazione imposte](nav:tax-return) resources to understand federal deadlines and procedures.

item.title: Geneva Airport is an engine for the region, worth 3.3 billion
item.description: Study Infras quantifies CHF 3.3 billion in added value, 22,000 jobs and impact on the entire Swiss economy. 17.8 million passengers were handled in 2025.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Infras study estimates 3.3 billion CHF in added value for Geneva-Cointrin Airport - In 2025, 17.8 million passengers handled, triple the original capacity of 5 million - Generates approximately 22,000 direct and indirect jobs - New flights to Singapore and São Paulo under study
## Key facts - **What**: Economic study on the impact of Geneva-Cointrin Airport - Who: Infras (Zurich-based consultancy) and Jean-François de Saussure (director of Genève Aéroport) - Amount: 3.3 billion CHF total added value; 1.9 billion for Canton Geneva - When: Study published today; 2025 passenger traffic data - Where: Geneva-Cointrin Airport and the Swiss national economy
Today's published study by Zurich-based consultancy Infras precisely quantifies the role of Geneva-Cointrin Airport as a pillar of the national economy. The annual added value generated reaches 3.3 billion Swiss francs, with nearly 2 billion directly falling within Canton Geneva.
Jean-François de Saussure, director of Genève Aéroport, emphasized in a press conference the strategic importance of air connectivity for businesses and international Geneva. The city hosts numerous international organizations, and the airport remains the essential gateway.
The numbers are impressive. In 2025, the airport handled 17.8 million travelers — a figure that triples the original capacity of 5 million for which it was designed. The traffic supports approximately 22,000 jobs within the airport ecosystem and related sectors.
### Extended impact on Swiss economy
The economic influence of the airport extends beyond the canton's borders. The study calculates that over 550 million Swiss francs of added value are distributed in the neighboring French region, while the rest of Switzerland benefits from an additional 770 million. Business aviation and cargo traffic form separate pillars: 330 and 350 million Swiss francs of economic impact, respectively, with approximately 96,000 tons of cargo transiting annually.
International organizations welcome 4,600 protocol delegations and host 6,000 conferences a year at airport facilities and surrounding areas. This flow of diplomatic missions and multilateral meetings creates a stable demand for international connectivity and specialized services. ### Expansion Strategy Towards Emerging Markets
Geneva Airport is not content with the status quo. De Saussure has outlined a growth strategy focused on emerging markets, particularly Asia. Currently, the hub operates 147 routes served by 57 airlines. Two new direct connections are under study: one to Singapore and one to São Paulo, Brazil.
The most evident signal of the geopolitical shift in air traffic flows is the enhancement of capacity towards China. Weekly flights to the Dragon have been increased to seven frequencies. The result is tangible: passengers generated from China now exceed those directed towards the United States. This imbalance reflects the evolution of global economic geopolitics and the increasing importance of Asian markets for Switzerland.
For those living or working in Switzerland, this expansion has a direct practical relevance. More routes to Asia mean shorter travel times for Swiss entrepreneurs operating in that continent, and better connection opportunities for multinational corporations based in the country. The [new job announcements in the airport and logistics sector](nav:jobs) related to the opening of Singapore and São Paulo will offer opportunities for specialized profiles.
### The Paradox of Capacity: Overloaded Infrastructure and Continuous Growth
One of the paradoxes faced by Genève Aéroport is the discrepancy between theoretical capacity and actual traffic. The facility was designed for 5 million annual passengers. In 2025, the volume reached 17.8 million, exceeding the original projections by over 250%. This structural stress has not hindered growth — on the contrary, the airport continues to expand its services and geographical coverage.
The figure suggests that Switzerland's critical infrastructures, if well-managed, can adapt to demand exceeding initial expectations. However, it also raises a question about long-term sustainability: to what extent is it possible to increase traffic without significant modernization? Nevertheless, Geneva's current capacity to handle nearly triple the expected volume demonstrates the robustness of the infrastructure and the efficiency of operational management.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### What does it mean for Swiss employment and development
The 22,000 jobs supported directly and indirectly by Geneva Airport are spread across a wide range of professional profiles: ground staff (ground handlers, security, maintenance), commercial staff (ticket, reception), and specialists (technical maintenance, cargo management). The expected growth of new international connections — Singapore, São Paulo, and consolidation towards China — suggests that demand for employment in the sector will remain robust.
For those living in the Geneva region, Ticino or the rest of Switzerland, the airport remains an important source of employment opportunities. Profiles sought include aircraft maintenance technicians, logistics specialists, loading/unloading operators, multilingual reception staff, and international conference managers. The [job opportunities in the transport and logistics sector](nav:jobs) related to the airport's expansion are expected to grow in the coming years.
### The airport as a multiplier of national connectivity
The relevance of Geneva Airport to Switzerland is not merely local. Air connectivity is a critical factor for the country's international competitiveness. When international organizations, multinational companies, and business travelers can count on seven weekly flights to China, or when new corridors to Singapore and Brazil emerge, the entire Switzerland benefits in terms of commercial and diplomatic attractiveness.
The Infras study formalizes what economic operators already know: an efficient airport is a multiplier of regional and national growth. The 770 million Swiss francs in added value generated in the rest of Switzerland — outside Geneva and the neighboring French region — demonstrate that the benefits are not geographically concentrated, but spread across the entire Swiss economic fabric.
For companies operating in the international arena, the expansion of Geneva Airport's connectivity represents a concrete strategic advantage: more routes, more frequencies, lower transport and logistics costs. Inquiring about the [Swiss plans for international transport and mobility](nav:transport) allows for a better understanding of how critical infrastructure influences business opportunities and daily life in the country.

item.title: Lucerne driving licence: conversion and exams
item.description: Procedure for converting the foreign licence in the Canton of Lucerne: theoretical and practical examination, compulsory courses, traffic office.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Foreign license conversion requires documentation and passing exams in the Canton of Lucerne - Theoretical and practical exams are mandatory for foreign licenses not automatically recognized - Mandatory courses to attend according to cantonal regulations
## Key facts - **What**: Conversion of foreign driving license in the Canton of Lucerne - Where: Canton of Lucerne, Switzerland - Who: Residents and workers with a foreign driving license - Procedure: Documentation + theoretical exam + practical exam + courses - Authority: Road Traffic Office of the Canton of Lucerne - Validity: Swiss driving license valid nationwide and abroad
Anyone moving to the Canton of Lucerne or starting to work in the region with a foreign driving license must undergo a conversion procedure regulated by cantonal rules. The procedure is not automatic: it requires passing theoretical and practical exams, as well as completing mandatory courses according to the current cantonal requirements.
The Road Traffic Office of the Canton of Lucerne manages all phases of the conversion. Anyone wishing to drive legally in Swiss territory with a foreign license must first obtain cantonal recognition, which depends on the country of origin of the license and compliance with Swiss road safety standards.
### When the conversion obligation kicks in
The conversion becomes mandatory at the time of registration in the residents' register of the Canton of Lucerne. It is not possible to drive legally with only a foreign license for an indefinite period: the cantonal authorities set a deadline by which the conversion application must be submitted. Delaying the procedure involves the risk of administrative sanctions and the invalidation of the foreign license for driving in Switzerland. ### Theoretical and practical exams
The theoretical exam in the Canton of Lucerne verifies knowledge of Swiss traffic regulations, road signs, and specific cantonal rules. The test is normally conducted in written or computerized form, with multiple-choice questions. Those who pass the theoretical exam can proceed to the practical exam, which evaluates actual driving skills: maneuvers, vehicle control, adherence to signals, behavior in complex traffic situations.
Candidates must present themselves with a suitable vehicle and an authorized companion during the practical test. The examiner from the Road Traffic Office accompanies the candidate on a standardized route and evaluates driving competence according to uniform criteria established by cantonal regulations. Those who do not pass the exam can retake the test after a waiting period set by the Canton.
### Mandatory courses and specializations
According to Lucerne cantonal regulations, some candidates must attend mandatory courses before or parallel to taking the exams. These courses cover road safety, Swiss traffic laws, behavior in case of an accident, and proper vehicle use. The duration and content of the courses depend on the candidate's profile and any gaps identified in the initial assessment by the Road Traffic Office.
In Switzerland, and thus in the Canton of Lucerne, road traffic is governed by very strict principles of civil liability. Drivers must demonstrate a thorough knowledge of federal and cantonal regulations, regardless of where they obtained their original license. Mandatory courses ensure that all drivers reach a uniform and traceable safety standard.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Step-by-step procedure
**Step 1: Gather documentation** Present yourself at the Road Traffic Office of the Canton of Lucerne with your passport or identity document, the original driving license (in the original language or translated by a certified translator), the residence certificate in the Canton, and the application form for conversion. The office communicates the complete and official list of required documentation during the first interview.
Step 2: Take the theoretical exam Under the guidance of the office, register for the theoretical exam. The date is communicated after verification of the documentation. Prepare with the educational material provided by the Road Traffic Office, available at the office or in an online version.
Step 3: Pass the practical exam After passing the theoretical exam, book the practical exam. Present yourself with a vehicle compliant with Swiss standards and an authorized companion according to the cantonal provisions. The examiner evaluates the driving in real traffic situations.
Step 4: Complete any mandatory courses If required, attend the courses indicated by the Road Traffic Office. The courses are normally held in a classroom or at authorized training centers and have a variable duration depending on the type of course.
Step 5: Pick up the converted license Once all exams are passed and courses completed, the Road Traffic Office issues the Swiss driving license in the name of the Canton of Lucerne. The license is valid throughout the national territory and in countries adhering to the European Union and the European Free Trade Association (EFTA).
### Contacts and timing The Road Traffic Office of the Canton of Lucerne is the sole authority competent for all phases of the conversion. Contact them for precise information on deadlines, actual costs, educational materials, and available exam dates. Opening hours and contact details are available on the official website of the Canton of Lucerne.
Do not wait for the official recall to start the procedure: the sooner you submit the application, the sooner you complete the conversion and obtain the right to drive legally in the Canton. Those who drive with an expired foreign license or without authorization risk significant administrative sanctions and the invalidation of the vehicle insurance contract, with serious consequences for civil liability.

item.title: Buying a house in Canton Lucerne: mortgage and tax guide
item.description: How real estate purchase works in the Canton of Lucerne: procedure, taxation, sustainability of the mortgage and notarial costs according to Swiss legislation.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Real estate purchase in Switzerland follows standard federal procedures and individual cantonal taxes. - The transfer tax is set by each canton at three levels: federal, cantonal, and municipal. - Banks assess mortgage sustainability according to standardized national debt-to-income criteria.
## Key facts - **What**: Legal procedure for real estate purchase regulated at the cantonal and municipal level - Where: Canton of Lucerne (procedure replicable in every Swiss canton) - Who: Buyer, seller, mortgage bank, public notary - Levels of government: Confederation + Canton of Lucerne + municipalities of Lucerne - Banking criteria: Standardized national debt-to-income ratio, required own funds - Tax burdens: Transfer tax, registration fee, notary fees
Buying a house in the Canton of Lucerne requires navigating a tax system structured at three levels of government: federal, cantonal, and municipal. Switzerland does not impose maximum or minimum prices for housing; the real estate market is entirely liberal and free from state price controls. Those wishing to purchase a property must, however, consider several mandatory burdens: the transfer tax (transfer of real estate ownership), notary fees, and registration costs with the cantonal administration.
The first decisive step is to verify the sustainability of the mortgage with a Swiss bank. Banks apply standardized national criteria to assess whether a borrower can afford the financing based on their gross income and existing debts. Although it is not a mandatory federal legal requirement, this assessment is a well-established banking practice and represents a sine qua non condition for access to real estate credit.
### The role of the notary and the legal procedure
In the Canton of Lucerne, as in the rest of Switzerland, real estate transactions must be notarized by a public notary. The notary is not a simple private intermediary: they are a public officer who authenticates the contract, verifies the identity and legitimacy of the parties, registers the property in the cantonal land registry, and calculates the taxes due according to the current legislation. Notary fees vary based on the purchase price; there is no single federal tariff, as each canton sets its own tariff guidelines.
The transfer tax (real estate transfer tax) is entirely managed by the cantons and municipalities. The Canton of Lucerne, like most Swiss cantons, applies a tax on the exchange and transfer of real estate ownership. This is a cantonal and municipal tax; the Confederation does not apply a federal tax on these transfers. ### Mortgage sustainability and banking criteria
The central question for those wishing to buy a house is: how much can I afford to borrow? In Switzerland, there is no mandatory federal debt ceiling imposed by law, but banks apply a standardized criterion widespread in the sector: the ratio between debt service (annual mortgage payment plus other recognized fixed expenses) and gross income should not exceed a predetermined threshold. This criterion varies slightly between banking institutions, but national practice is consistent and uniformly applied by all major Swiss banks.
A second fundamental element in credit assessment is the requirement for own funds (equity). Swiss banks generally require that the buyer has a minimum percentage of equity, usually ranging between 10% and 30% of the total purchase price. This is not a mandatory federal law, but it represents a widespread banking condition adopted as a standard by the Swiss credit sector. Own funds can come from personal savings, inheritances, or withdrawals from the third pillar (3a), subject to certain legal conditions established by the federation.
The transfer tax represents a significant burden in the overall planning of the purchase and must be considered in the preliminary budget. Although the Canton of Lucerne sets the basic cantonal rate, the final cost depends on the cadastral value of the property and the geographical location (Lucerne municipalities can apply their own multipliers). It is essential to obtain a correct estimate of the cadastral real estate value before signing the final contract, as this affects both the bank financing (the bank conducts an internal appraisal of the property) and the taxes due.
Finally, there are additional costs that add to the mortgage and taxes: registration fees in the land register, technical costs (cadastral appraisal, surveyor, engineer), and notary fees calculated in proportion to the price. The notary provides a detailed preliminary estimate of these costs, allowing the buyer to plan the total budget of the operation and to realistically evaluate the economic and financial convenience of the purchase.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### How to proceed: practical steps
The typical process begins with searching for a property on the free market in Lucerne and submitting a non-binding offer to the seller. Once the suitable house is found and the price is negotiated, the parties sign a preliminary contract (often referred to as a 'purchase agreement' or 'preliminary contract'); at this point, the buyer must formally notify the bank of their intention to finance the purchase.
The bank initiates the mortgage application process: it evaluates the buyer's gross income (over the last 2-3 years), their creditworthiness, the property value (through an internal appraisal conducted by certified bank appraisers), and calculates the maximum amount that can be financed according to federal sustainability criteria and the bank's own criteria. If the applicant is eligible, the bank issues a mortgage offer with current interest rates, loan term (usually 10, 15, or 20 years), and specific contractual conditions. The buyer has the right to accept the proposed terms or negotiate with the bank.
Parallel to the banking procedure, the buyer must contact a public notary in the Canton of Lucerne for the execution of the final purchase contract. The notary verifies the property and identity documents, calculates the transfer tax and related fees, and prepares everything necessary for the official signing in their presence as a public official. The signing of the final contract usually takes place 2-4 weeks after the formal agreement with the bank.
Post-signing, the notary assumes the following responsibilities: - Registers the contract with the Lucerne cantonal and municipal authorities - Submits the transfer tax declaration to the cantonal tax administration - Verifies the payment of the transfer tax and all related fees - Orders the transfer of ownership in the cantonal land register and cadastre
The entire operation typically takes 6-10 weeks from the preliminary contract to the final registration of the property in the land register. During this period, the buyer must ensure full financing: gather and deposit their own funds with the notary and coordinate the bank's mortgage disbursement with the notarial procedure.
To simplify preliminary financial planning, it is advisable to use the [mortgage and tax calculators](nav:calculator) available online, which allow for the simulation of different financing scenarios based on the estimated purchase price, available own funds, and current interest rates in the Swiss market.

item.title: Buying a house in Lucerne: mortgage and taxes
item.description: Buying a property in the Canton of Lucerne requires fiscal-financial skills: transfer taxes, sustainable mortgage, notary fees. Operating Guide 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Purchase of a house in Switzerland: taxation on 3 levels (federal, cantonal, municipal) - Mortgage loan requires sufficient own funds and bank sustainability verification - Tax on cantonal-communal transfers and notary fees are additional costs - National rule: maximum mortgage fee 20% of annual gross income
## Key facts - **What**: Purchase of residential property and mortgage lending - When: Continuous procedure; registration with cantonal land registry office - Where: Canton Lucerne (tax rates vary by municipality) - Who: Buyer, bank, notary, land registry office - Taxes: Cantonal-communal transfer tax, notary fees (variable amounts)
Homebuyers in Switzerland face a tax structure divided into three levels: federal, cantonal and municipal. In the Canton of Lucerne, as in every Swiss canton, the transfer tax affects the real estate transaction with a local rate whose amount depends on the sale price and the rules of the canton and the municipality of location. In addition to the direct purchase costs, the buyer must count notary fees, bank fees for the mortgage and the property appraisal. Taking out a mortgage loan also involves rigorous bank checks on the financial sustainability of the borrower, assessing income, AVS/AI (compulsory social security) and LAMal (compulsory health insurance for Swiss residents).
Swiss taxation ### Procedure for buying and selling and the roles of the parties involved
The purchase of a property in Switzerland is concluded with a public notarial deed deposited with the land register of the canton. The buyer and seller sign the purchase agreement in the presence of the notary, who verifies the legality of the transaction, the contractual capacity of the parties, the absence of encumbrances on the property (previous mortgages, seizures, rights of pre-emption) and compliance with municipal building regulations. The notary also ensures the deposit of funds in a blocked account in the name of the buyer until the property is fully transferred, providing legal protection to both parties according to federal law (Code of Obligations, articles 253 and following).
The typical procedure consists of sequential phases:
**Pre-qualification of the mortgage**: The buyer contacts one or more banks to receive a preliminary, non-binding mortgage attestation, indicating the maximum credit available based on declared incomes.
Non-binding offer: Once the desired property is identified, the buyer signs an offer to the seller, usually conditional on the bank's approval of the mortgage.
Property appraisal: The bank entrusts an independent technical expert with the valuation of the property. The appraisal value determines the maximum mortgage, typically calculated as a percentage of 60–80% of the estimated value.
Mortgage approval: Once the appraisal report is received, the bank formally communicates the mortgage approval and the terms (interest rate, amortization, duration of the financing).
Drafting of the notarial deed: The buyer and seller go to the notary's office. The notary drafts the purchase deed, verifies the property documents with the land register, receives the buyer's funds and the mortgage in a blocked account in the name of the buyer, and proceeds with the registration at the cantonal land register office.
Land registry registration: The notary deposits the deed with the land register office. Once the transaction is registered, the property is in the name of the buyer and the mortgage is registered as a guarantee on the property.
Mortgage disbursement: The bank disburses the final mortgage, which is transferred directly to the notary. The notary pays the funds to the seller and returns any excess funds to the buyer (if the mortgage exceeds the total purchase costs).
### Bank criteria for evaluating creditworthiness
Swiss banks use standardized criteria to evaluate a mortgage. The first element is the value of the property, determined by technical appraisal. The mortgage typically covers 60–80% of the appraisal value; the remaining 20–40% must come from the buyer's own funds (own capital or deposit). Some credit institutions accept different percentages (up to 90% mortgage) for clients with high creditworthiness, certain incomes, and minimal existing debts.
The buyer's financial capacity is evaluated based on: pay slips from the last 2–3 years, bank statements, federal and cantonal tax returns (IFD and local taxes), credit history with Swiss banking scoring services. If the buyer resides in Switzerland, the bank also verifies the mandatory contributions to AVS/AI and LAMal premiums, which represent deductions from the net available income for calculating sustainability. The monthly installment is calculated based on an interest rate set by the bank, reflecting market conditions (reference rates of the Swiss National Bank – BNS/SNB) and the buyer's individual credit rating.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Pre-purchase operational checklist
Before proceeding with the purchase of a property in the Canton of Lucerna, the buyer should follow these preparatory steps:
1. **Obtain a preliminary mortgage certificate**: Contact at least two banks to receive a preliminary mortgage certificate (non-binding, typical validity 2–4 months). This document allows you to negotiate with the seller with awareness of the available funds.
2. Analyze personal budget: Carefully verify stable income over the last 2–3 years, accumulated own funds, current debts (car loans, personal loans, credit cards), fixed monthly expenses (rent, LAMal, various insurances).
3. Consult a cantonal tax advisor: Inform yourself about the specific rates of the transfer tax in the Canton of Lucerna and in the municipality where the property is located. Verify the possible existence of benefits for first-time buyers, tax deductions or exemptions.
4. Verify the status of the property with the land registry: Request an extract from the cantonal land registry to ensure the absence of seizures, previous mortgages, rights of pre-emption or municipal constraints that could hinder the transfer of the property.
5. Conduct an independent technical inspection: Hire a technical expert (not appointed by the bank) to verify the structural condition, structural suitability, building compliance and the possible need for maintenance or renovation interventions that will impact the value and future costs.
### Step-by-step towards purchase
Weeks 1–4 – Mortgage prequalification: Contact at least two banks and request a preliminary mortgage certificate. Prepare: copy of federal and cantonal tax returns (IFD) for the last 2 years, bank statements for the last 3 months, employment certificate with gross monthly salary, detailed list of current debts. The preliminary certificate will have a validity of 2–4 months.
Weeks 5–12 – Property search and offer: Identify the desired property through real estate agents or search platforms. Sign a non-binding written offer, conditional on mortgage approval. Communicate to the agent the maximum offer amount and the realistic timing of the transaction closure. Request a preliminary report on the property from the notary to identify any constraints or encumbrances.
Weeks 13–20 – Mortgage approval and notary: Once formal mortgage approval is obtained from the bank, contact the notary for the drafting of the sales deed. The notary will request: copy of the mortgage certificate, identification of the seller (personal extract), property documentation (title deed, cadastral plan, cantonal energy certificate if mandatory). Set the date of the signing at the notary's office. In the days preceding the signature, the notary receives the buyer's funds and deposits them in a blocked account in the buyer's name, as prescribed by federal law (art. 253 ff. Code of Obligations).
Week 21 – Registration and data transmission: The notary proceeds with the registration of the deed with the cantonal land registry office. Once the transaction is registered, the notary communicates the transfer to the bank. The bank disburses the mortgage (final tranching) and transfers it directly to the notary, who pays the proceeds to the seller.
Week 22+ – Post-purchase phase: The buyer receives a copy of the registered deed, property documents and the corresponding land registry extract (copy extract). The bank communicates the operational details of the mortgage (monthly installment in CHF, TAN/TAEG, amortization plan). The buyer must obligatorily take out fire insurance on the property, as prescribed by Swiss cantonal regulations.
### Calculation tools and decision support
To estimate the sustainability of a mortgage and visualize the impact of the monthly installment on your personal budget, you can use the [mortgage calculator](nav:calculator). This tool allows you to simulate different interest rate, amortization and mortgage amount scenarios, providing a realistic estimate of monthly expenses and compatibility with your net income.
A tax advisor specialized in Swiss cantonal law can provide you with detailed information on transfer tax rates in the Canton of Lucerna, possible benefits for first-time buyers, exemption amounts, special deductions and administrative procedures with the municipal tax office.

item.title: Family doctors criticize Tardoc tariff
item.description: Tardoc does not re-evaluate family medicine and increases outpatient costs. The MFE association asks the Federal Council to avoid a linear devaluation.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Tardoc has not revalued family medicine as expected by decision-makers - Outpatient costs have increased significantly, imbalance in primary care - mfe association rejects a linear devaluation of all specialties
## Key facts - **What**: new outpatient medical tariff (Tardoc) - Who: Swiss Association of Family Doctors and Pediatricians (mfe) - Status: family medicine not revalued; outpatient costs increased - Source: Monika Reber, co-president mfe - Body: Federal Council (requirements for cost neutrality)
The Swiss Association of Family Doctors and Pediatricians (mfe) strongly criticizes the new Tardoc medical tariff. In today's communication, the organization denounces the failure to revalue family medicine, a widespread expectation among federal and cantonal political decision-makers. Instead of economically recognizing the value of primary care, the new system has resulted in a significant increase in costs in the Swiss outpatient sector, creating a structural imbalance.
### The tariff imbalance risks worsening
The situation is even more critical in certain cantons, where family medicine has even suffered a devaluation. Only pediatricians and general practitioners see a slight improvement within the new tariff. This creates a growing imbalance at the expense of basic care, the sector that ensures primary care for patients in the Swiss healthcare system.
The co-president of mfe, Monika Reber, states in the press release: "Overall, the Tardoc system shows a considerable increase in costs, while the revaluation of family doctors, requested by all parties, has not taken place." The association rejects a solution that would involve a linear devaluation of all medical specialties, aware that this scenario would further worsen the situation of basic care and the overall balance of the outpatient healthcare system. ### The cost of family medicine in crisis
The tariff imbalance created by Tardoc represents a concrete challenge for the future of the Swiss healthcare system. When outpatient costs increase significantly but family medicine does not benefit economically, a structural disincentive is created that could discourage family doctors from remaining in this professional field. The shortage of family doctors is already a recognized problem in many Swiss cantons, and the new tariff schedule risks worsening this situation.
The overall increase in costs in the outpatient sector is not invisible to the rest of the system. Due to these increases, the Federal Council has set cost neutrality requirements in the healthcare sector. This means that any cost increases will have to be neutralized through subsequent tariff adjustments, creating a chain reaction that affects all medical specialties and further complicates the regulatory framework.
### Implications for health insurance premiums and the cost of living
For those living in Switzerland, the most direct impact could be reflected in the premiums of the [LAMal](<nav:health>), the mandatory health insurance. If outpatient costs continue to rise without a corresponding tariff revision that compensates for the increase, health insurance funds will face increasingly narrow margins. This can translate into upward pressure on premiums, as insurers must ensure full coverage of outpatient medical services.
The tariff imbalance highlights a fundamental tension in the Swiss healthcare system: on the one hand, the need to maintain cost neutrality at the federal level; on the other hand, the need to ensure adequate economic recognition for all medical branches, particularly for primary care, which forms the foundation of healthcare. The mfe asks the Federal Council to find a balance that avoids a linear devaluation and ensures the sustainability of primary care.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### How to monitor tariff changes in your canton
The tariff adjustment process is ongoing, and the decisions of the Federal Council will have direct implications for residents. Those living in Switzerland can follow the evolution of the situation through official channels: the UFSP (Federal Office of Public Health) website publishes information on tariff revisions and federal consultations. Medical associations such as mfe continue to participate in negotiations and make their positions public through regular press releases.
It is useful to stay informed about tariff developments as they indirectly affect the healthcare services available in your canton and potentially the costs of access. If you notice changes in the costs of basic medical consultations in your area, it could be related to the current tariff adjustments being made by the federal administration.
### Practical tools and resources for further exploration
For those who wish to delve deeper into the cost of their health coverage, there are online platforms that allow you to compare the premiums of different health insurance providers. The official LAMal resource offers an overview of premiums by canton and region, as well as information on any subsidies for premium payments. The mfe association remains the reference point for family doctors who wish to understand the implications of the new tariff system on their professional practice.
Patients who have specific questions about the coverage of certain outpatient services can contact their family doctor or their health insurance provider for clarification. Always keep a copy of your LAMal policy and consult the official insurance website for any updates on coverage and deductibles. For a more accurate estimate of how healthcare-related living costs could impact your annual budget, use our [calculator](<nav:calculator>) to simulate different medical expense scenarios.

item.title: Apprenticeship in Lucerne: a practical guide
item.description: Search for internship, salary, social contributions and professional maturity: here's how to orient yourself in Swiss dual training in Lucerne.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Dual apprenticeship: 3-4 years between company and vocational school - Maximum hours 45-50 hours/week, 4-5 weeks of guaranteed vacation - Increasing salary and social contributions from the first day
## Key facts - **What**: Professional training (AFC) in a dual system - Where: Canton of Lucerne, companies and vocational schools - Who: Young people from 15 years old with compulsory education completed - Duration: 3-4 years depending on the profession - Start: Search 1-2 years before the start date - Protection: Federal labor law applies to all apprentices
Apprenticeship in Switzerland is the most widespread professional training path after compulsory schooling. In the Canton of Lucerne, the system operates on a dual basis: the young apprentice spends 60-70% of the time in the company (practical training with a qualified trainer) and 30-40% in a vocational school (theoretical lessons and general culture). This model combines practical skills and knowledge, ensuring that the labor market has figures ready for employment.
The search for the internship usually begins during the penultimate or last year of middle school. The main channels are the official job search sites, direct contact with companies in the sector of interest, training fairs organized by the canton, and school guidance offices. In the Canton of Lucerne, the cantonal vocational training office provides support to both young people and host companies in the matching process between demand and supply.
### The internship contract: rights and duties
The internship contract is the fundamental legal instrument that regulates the relationship between the apprentice, the trainer, and the company. It must be drawn up in writing and contains essential information: total duration, start date, gross monthly salary, weekly working hours, vocational school days, insurances, rights, and duties of both parties.
The trainer commits to providing professional training according to the cantonal training objectives, to carrying out periodic checks of progress, to paying the agreed salary, and to issuing the internship certificate at the end. The apprentice commits to regularly attending lessons and practical training in the company, to respecting the company regulations, to performing the assigned tasks diligently, and to participating in the final exams.
### Legal protection and rights of the apprentice
During the internship, the apprentice enjoys federal legal protection. The maximum working hours are 45 hours per week in the industry, offices, and commerce sectors (50 hours in other sectors). Minimum vacations are guaranteed: 4 weeks per year for apprentices over 20 years old, 5 weeks for under 20 (some cantons and collective sectors provide 5 uniform weeks). Breaks and weekly rest are mandatory according to the federal labor law.
In case of termination, the notice period is 1 month during the first year; from the second year onwards, it increases to 2 months. In cases of serious non-compliance (e.g., systematic violation of training duties), immediate termination with documented justification is possible. During the internship period, the apprentice accumulates mandatory contributions to the federal social security systems (AVS/AHV, unemployment insurance), ensuring protection in case of future illness, injury, or unemployment. ### Compensation and Salary Dynamics
The apprentice's compensation is not set at the federal level: each canton, sector, and company determines the monthly amount independently. In the Canton of Lucerne, as in other Swiss cantons, the salary range for apprentices varies depending on the profession and the chosen VET pathway. Generally, compensation increases year by year: the first year is lower, the second and third years increase progressively, reaching amounts closer to the salary of a qualified professional in the fourth year. Some sectors (e.g., crafts, manufacturing industry, retail trade) have collective wages agreed upon between employers' associations and unions, which establish uniform minimums for the category.
During the apprenticeship, compensation is subject to federal, cantonal, and municipal taxation, according to the Swiss three-tier system. Each canton has its own tax rates, and each municipality acts as a multiplier on the cantonal level. An apprentice residing in the Canton of Lucerne pays federal direct tax based on income (with deductible allowances for young people and students), then Lucerne cantonal tax, and finally a municipal tax on top of the cantonal base.
### Mandatory Social Contributions
From the first month of the apprenticeship, the apprentice is enrolled in the Swiss social security systems. The gross monthly amount received is subject to precise deductions:
- **AVS/AHV and disability insurance (AI)**: 5.3% borne by the employee (apprentice); the employer pays the complementary 5.3%, for a total of 10.6%. These contributions guarantee the right to old-age pension, disability pension, and survivor's benefits. - Unemployment insurance (AD) and insolvency insurance (AC): 1.1% borne by the employee up to an annual maximum (the exact amount varies each year, consult the cantonal office for 2026). Covers protection in case of involuntary job loss. - Accident insurance (LAINF/LAA): 0.7–1.5% borne by the employer, depending on the sector. The apprentice does not pay direct contributions but is automatically covered for work-related accidents and occupational diseases. - Professional pension fund (LPP/BVG): If the company has a pension fund, the apprentice might not be enrolled during the first year (depends on company and cantonal instructions). Some cantons require enrollment from the second year or with a minimum salary threshold.
💡 The sum of these contributions amounts to about 12-15% of the gross salary. The exact percentages for AVS/AI and AD/AC are fixed according to federal laws, while LAINF and LPP vary depending on the sector and company. Consult the Lucerne cantonal office for specific details and applicable amounts for 2026.
### Income Tax and Deductions
The federal direct tax on employment income is progressive and depends on the tax rate of the civil status and asset situation. For an apprentice, usual deductions include: deduction for dependent employment income (amount not specified for 2026, consult AFC/ESTV), travel and accommodation expenses (if necessary to reach the workplace and school), and health insurance premiums (LAMal/KVG). Health insurance must be taken out within 3 months of the start of the apprenticeship (if not already in possession). LAMal premiums depend on the canton, geographical region, age, and chosen deductible (for adults: CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 or 2500). In the Canton of Lucerne, the canton provides [subsidies (cantonal contributions) for premiums](nav:health) for young people and low-income individuals, reducing the economic burden.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Professional Maturity: The Upgrade After AFC
Upon completion of the AFC apprenticeship (3-4 years), the apprentice receives the professional apprentice certificate (Lehrbrief), a nationally recognized document that allows them to practice their profession with verified qualifications. Many apprentices choose to complete a professional maturity program, which can be obtained in parallel during the internship (integrated part-time model) or after the AFC certificate (post-diploma professional maturity). Professional maturity adds theoretical skills and opens access to specialized university studies at universities of applied sciences (UAS), or in some cases, cantonal universities. In the Canton of Lucerne, institutions such as the Berufsfachschule Luzern offer integrated or post-AFC professional maturity programs.
Other apprentices continue with post-apprenticeship specializations (continuing education), international certifications in their field, or directly enter the job market with a qualified apprentice salary. Opportunities for further education depend on the individual's profile, professional interests, and access requirements for subsequent training.
### Step-by-Step Procedure: From Search to Completion
The search and application process begins about 18 months before the actual start. Consult the cantonal internship search portal, visit training fairs, and contact companies of interest directly. Prepare a CV and cover letter in line with industry expectations. The company evaluates the candidate and, if suitable, proposes a start date and details of the internship contract.
Once selected, the contract must be signed by the apprentice, parents (if a minor), and the trainer. It includes: duration, monthly salary, hours, training assignments, rights, and duties of both parties. The Canton of Lucerne's training office automatically enrolls the apprentice in the relevant vocational school (mandatory), and the company registers the apprentice with the AVS/AHV offices, unemployment insurance, and pension fund providers (if applicable).
During the internship, the apprentice regularly attends school lessons and practices in the company, completes the training journal (Ausbildungsjournal), executes practical projects, and participates in progress checks. At the end of the program, the apprentice takes a practical skills exam (at the company or cantonal exam center) and a theoretical knowledge verification (at the vocational school). Upon passing, they receive the nationally recognized professional apprentice certificate, valid as a credential in the job market.
### Practical Tools and Resources
To calculate your net salary considering mandatory social contributions (AVS/AI, AD/AC, LAINF), three-level taxation, and allowed deductions, use our [salary calculator](nav:calculator). If you want to plan your savings during the internship and understand the impact of LPP/BVG on your future pension, consult our guides on [pension and LPP](nav:pension). Finally, the internship search is a gradual and strategic process: use our [job search engine](nav:jobs) to discover open positions in the Canton of Lucerne and the rest of Switzerland, with filters for sector, duration, and location.

item.title: Apprenticeship in Lucerne: contract, salary and maturity
item.description: How to find an apprenticeship position in the Canton of Lucerne, what the apprenticeship contract must contain and how to obtain professional maturity: practical guide.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Apprenticeship: 3-4 year path between school and company - Mandatory written contract with monthly salary - Recognized diploma at the end of the path (professional maturity) - Opportunities for all professional sectors
## Key facts - **What**: Dual training system (work + vocational school) - Where: Canton of Lucerna (available in all sectors) - Duration: Typically 3-4 years - When: Usually starts after compulsory schooling - Outcome: Federal Vocational Baccalaureate (VET) or specialized diploma (CFC)
Apprenticeship represents in Switzerland one of the main professional training paths for young people. In the Canton of Lucerna, as in all Swiss cantons, the system works according to a dual model: the apprentice works in a company on Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, while attending vocational school on Thursday and Friday (the proportions vary by sector).
The first step is to find a company willing to train an apprentice. Apprenticeship offers are published on national platforms, on the canton websites, and at regional professional guidance offices. In the canton of Lucerna, the Professional Guidance Office provides lists of training companies and available offers. To discover the available apprenticeship positions, consult the [job offers](nav:jobs) in your canton.
### Structure and duration of the apprenticeship
The typical duration of an apprenticeship is three or four years, depending on the sector and the chosen level of specialization. Some sectors (such as construction) provide a three-year path, while others (such as pharmacy or IT) require four years. During the apprenticeship, the apprentice follows a practical training program in the company and a theoretical program at the vocational school.
The apprentice is considered a full-fledged worker. This means that during the apprenticeship, all regulations on rest, holidays, health, and workplace safety provided by federal and cantonal legislation apply. The minimum holidays are 5 weeks per year for those under 20, and at least 4 weeks for adults. ### Apprenticeship contract and remuneration
A written contract is mandatory for every apprenticeship. The contract must specify the training company, the apprentice, the profession taught, the duration of the internship, the weekly working hours, and the monthly salary. The contracting parties must sign the document, which represents the legal basis of the training relationship.
The apprentice's remuneration varies depending on the year of training. In the first year, the monthly salary is lower; it increases progressively in the following years. These amounts are set by collective labor agreements (CCL) for sector and canton. In the Canton of Lucerne, as in other cantons, employers operating in sectors regulated by CCL must comply with the minimum salary thresholds defined by the contract itself.
In addition to the gross salary, federal social contributions apply to the apprentice's remuneration: - AVS/AI/IPG: approximately 5.3% of the salary (at the apprentice's expense) - Unemployment insurance (AD): approximately 1.1% up to an annual maximum - Accident insurance (LAINF): at the employer's expense (rate 0.7–1.5% depending on the sector)
To calculate your net salary during the apprenticeship, you can use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) which takes into account all federal and cantonal contributions of the Canton of Lucerne.
### Pension and insurance aspects
An apprentice is NOT subject to professional pension contributions (LPP/BVG) during the internship, but is once hired as an employee. The apprentice must take out health insurance (LAMal) within 3 months of starting employment, choosing from the offers available in the Canton of Lucerne. Researching the most convenient health insurance fund is optional but recommended, considering that premiums vary between insurers. Many cantons offer subsidies to reduce the premium for low-income young people.
During the internship, the apprentice has the right to receive quality professional training, access to compulsory school courses, health and safety protection, and regular remuneration. The employer must provide the tools and knowledge necessary to acquire the skills provided for in the training program.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ### Professional maturity and diploma achievement
At the end of the apprenticeship, the apprentice must take the final exam to obtain the professional maturity diploma. This exam verifies the skills acquired both in practical business and in school education. The diploma (Federal Vocational Baccalaureate — VET, or Federal Vocational Education and Training Certificate — VET) is recognized nationally and opens the door to further continuing education paths.
After obtaining the diploma, the apprentice can directly enter the job market as a skilled worker or employee, or continue towards higher education (higher vocational school, advanced courses, master's). Those who wish to access university can attend a supplementary high school maturity.
### How to find an internship position in the Canton of Lucerne: step-by-step procedure
**Step 1: Initial research**
Visit the official internship search sites at the national and Canton of Lucerne levels. Dedicated platforms, professional association sites, and the professional orientation portal provide updated lists of companies looking for apprentices.
Step 2: Preparing the application
Write a short resume and a motivation letter showing your interest in the chosen sector. Contact the company directly to learn about the application methods. Many companies provide preliminary interviews or one or two-week 'trial internship' days to assess the suitability of the choice.
Step 3: Contract signing
Once the position is found, the employer and the apprentice sign the apprenticeship contract. The contract must be written, signed by both parties, and kept for the entire duration of the training.
Step 4: Enrollment in vocational school
The employer takes care of enrolling the apprentice in the vocational school competent for the Canton of Lucerne. This enrollment is administrative but fundamental.
Step 5: Start and progress
The apprentice starts work according to the established calendar and the school calendar of the vocational school. They attend school lessons and continue practical training in the company according to the four-year or three-year program.
To deepen the details on professional training in your canton, consult the [salary and contribution calculator](nav:calculator) to estimate the net monthly salary during the apprenticeship, and check the [job offers](nav:jobs) available for new apprentices in the Canton of Lucerne.

item.title: Natural reserves put to the test by drought
item.description: The summer drought hit the swamps hard, with water levels falling to critical levels in many areas.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Swiss wetlands have been hit by a severe drought - In some areas, the wetlands have dried up completely - Pro Natura's natural reserves have been put to the test
## Key facts - **What**: Summer drought that has affected wetlands and watercourses - When: Summer 2024 - Where: Wetland areas in Switzerland, including Rothenthurm (SZ) and Balmoos (LU) - Who: Pro Natura
This summer's heatwaves have put Swiss natural reserves to the test. The drought has particularly affected wetlands, watercourses, trees, and lakes, Pro Natura reported today.
### Effects on flora and fauna The consequences were particularly evident in the Rothenthurm (SZ) wetland area. "I have never seen the wetlands this dry since I took on the position in 2009," says Bastien Amez-Droz, project manager at Pro Natura, quoted in a statement.
The Svitto Forest Office, in collaboration with Pro Natura and some local construction companies, had carried out regeneration work to restore the water retention capacity. According to Amez-Droz, these areas remained wet at least until August, allowing dragonflies to lay eggs and newts to rest.
In the Balmoos (LU) high bog, the water level has dropped by 15-20 centimeters compared to normal. Even in this case, the worst could be avoided: "Without the renaturation work carried out last autumn, there would have been no more free water this summer," Amez-Droz continues.
In some Pro Natura natural reserves, such as in Martinet (JU), the brooks have completely dried up. In other regions, their flow has decreased, but the water has not disappeared, as in the protected areas of Gitzitobel (LU) or La Chaux-de-Brenleire, near Vanil Noir (FR).
### Impact on Ticino In Ticino, the summer heatwave has caused an exceptional proliferation of algae in the Muzzano pond. This has prevented light penetration and hindered the development of aquatic plants and animals.
"The pond suffers from an excessive load of nutrients due to the discharge of agricultural residues for several years in the past," explains Serena Britos Wiederkehr, manager of the Laghetto di Muzzano natural reserve. The excess of nutrients, particularly phosphorus, favor the proliferation of algae and cyanobacteria, a phenomenon further aggravated by the great heat, it is underlined.
Due to the unbearably high temperatures, in Ticino the pace of interventions in natural reserves has had to be slowed down, with consequent extension of the realization times, it is pointed out. ### Analysis of the effects of drought The summer drought had a significant impact on Swiss nature reserves, putting local flora and fauna at risk. Swamps, in particular, have been hit hard, with water levels falling to critical levels in many areas.
### Effects on the forest As for the state of the forests, it is very difficult to draw conclusions: only in one to five years we will see how many trees have survived, survived or are dying. Pro Natura considers the restoration of rainforests a "promising solution in the face of climate warming".
### Mitigation measures The authorities have taken several measures to mitigate the effects of the drought. These include works to regenerate marshes and peat bogs, which have made it possible to keep the areas humid and promote animal life.
### Impact on tourism The drought has also had a negative impact on tourism, with many nature reserves being closed to the public to ensure the safety of animals and plants.
### Future prospects Authorities are evaluating new strategies to address the challenges of climate change, with a particular focus on restoring natural reserves and sustainably managing water resources.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### Actions to be taken To address drought, it is important to adopt water conservation and nature reserve regeneration measures. Local authorities and organisations such as Pro Natura are working to implement renaturation projects that can help restore the ecosystem.
### Tips for residents Residents are encouraged to reduce the use of water for gardening and to report any instances of swamp drainage. It is important to be aware of the importance of natural reserves and their role in the management of water resources.
### Useful tools For more information and calculation tools, you can visit our [calcolatore di imposte](nav:calculator) to get an idea of your expenses and tax obligations. In addition, you can consult the section dedicated to the [costo della vita](nav:cost-of-living) to get an idea of the daily expenses and costs of maintaining the nature reserves.
*Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/riserve-naturali-messe-a-dura-prova-da-siccit%c3%a0/91999663)*
